reviewer: builder (the agent session that wrote the generator)
findings: Five storeys: a ground storey and four ribbon and band pairs on all four sides, as both perspective references show.

Each band reads as a main face under a projecting cap strip with a shadow line; an earlier sloped-sill profile and an earlier set-back strip were both rejected against enlarged crops of the references.
Roof plan matches the reference in footprint ratio, penthouse position, the rear east well, the walkway position and the roof items.
Ribbon glazing is a recessed bronze frame and glass with floors, ceilings, columns, rooms and desks behind; no pane is a flat card.
The entrance is a pair of glazed doors in the second bay from the east corner with a glazed draught lobby behind; the threshold is 35 mm above grade.
West flank and rear are complete service elevations with real openings; both are inferred and recorded as such.
Nothing floats: every roof item, the cooling unit and the door landing rest on a surface. Nothing sits below grade.
open_notes: The street reference shows far more penthouse above the parapet than the roof plan and oblique allow. Recorded as a source conflict; roof plan governs.
The walkway is a 9 m length with a glazed end and no support at the free end; the references run it to a neighbouring building.
Both perspective references place the walkway at the third storey, not the second where a +15 normally sits. Built as drawn.
Joints 30 mm wide break up into dashes in distant views; a renderer sampling effect, not a gap in the geometry.
Shadow edges under the soffit are stepped in close views: shadow-map resolution in the review renderer.
The walkway crown rises 70 mm into the cap strip of the band above it; to be made flush in the next candidate.
